title: JDBC Fundamentals
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of jdbc fundamentals and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—jdbc architecture—in a small, readable example.
Identify one failure, compatibility, security, or resource-management concern and describe a safe response.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study jdbc fundamentals with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you access database data safely with parameter binding, resource management, and transactions. In this lesson, focus on jdbc architecture and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Keep database work behind a data-access boundary. Use prepared statements for values, transactions for related changes, and try-with-resources to close statements, result sets, and connections. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect jdbc architecture with driver configuration before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: JDBC architecture
items.text: Keep database work behind a data-access boundary. Use prepared statements for values, transactions for related changes, and try-with-resources to close statements, result sets, and connections.

items.title: Driver configuration
items.text: Use Path and Files for modern file operations, choose byte or character APIs based on the data, and close resources reliably. Parse external files defensively because their contents may be incomplete or malformed.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Treat SQL as data access and use PreparedStatement for values. Database execution requires a configured JDBC driver and connection. For ordinary Java SE examples, use JDK 25, save a complete class as Main.java, and run `javac Main.java` followed by `java Main`. CodeLeaf does not execute Java in the browser; use a local JDK for these examples. Preview-only and configuration-file examples have their own version or filename notes.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original example, remove any temporary output files it created, and rerun the baseline case. Do not leave credentials, generated private data, or large test files in the project directory.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.

content.task: Try it yourself: model jdbc fundamentals with a local test database or a mocked boundary. Use parameters for values, define transaction boundaries, and verify that resources close when an error occurs.

common_mistakes.problem: Applying the rule from memory without checking its exact contract.
common_mistakes.why: Small differences in type, scope, API version, or input shape can change the result.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the relevant official API/language documentation and build a minimal reproducer.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only a single happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Boundary values and failures often reveal assumptions hidden by the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add an empty, boundary, or invalid case and state the expected behavior before running it.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify the actual cause of a different result.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one factor at a time and keep a short record of observed behavior.
